lr:n4:tatoeba-10049455.problem: Passes the TaughtSets gate only because sent:tatoeba-10049455 is dissected with grammar ['yo'] and the token とい carries no tag. The script やっといたよ and distractor うん、やっとくね both use the ~とく contraction of ~ておく, which the course registry teaches only at N3 (gram:n3-toku; gram:te-oku lists ておく only), so an N4 learner has not met the form. The level-clean pool has no real ~ておいた utterance to select instead. Corrected by expanding both to the taught ~ておく form. That edits the Tatoeba sentence, so the item becomes source edited, ai_generated, and must drop its sentence ref. Key and family unchanged: done favor, happy reply; the other two options stay wrong (asks for something already done / promises to do it).

ls:n4:015.problem: Two defensible keys. ~てもらって、ありがとうございました is common in natural spoken Japanese (it is the plain form of ~ていただいて、ありがとうございました, which is fully correct). Said to a teacher it is only a missing honorific, not a wrong thanks, so a test-taker can defend it next to the くださって key. Corrected replaces it with a request for something already received (教えてくださいませんか). That is wrong for the situation and is still a listening trap on くださって / ください. All grammar is taught at N4 (te-kudasai, masen-ka) and the kanji are clean.
